Export a Phytosociological Synoptic Table to Excel

Source: R/export_synoptic.R
export_synoptic.Rd

Exports a phytosociological synoptic table to a formatted Excel workbook, displaying diagnostic species in group-specific sections and the remaining species in a separate section. Species frequencies, Phi coefficients, association p-values, and dominance information are included.

Usage

export_synoptic(
  synoptic,
  file = "Tabella_sinottica.xlsx",
  min_frequency = 0,
  digits = 0,
  group_sizes = NULL
)

Arguments

synoptic

A data frame (or object coercible to a data frame), typically res$synoptic from synoptic_table(). It must contain the required diagnostic, dominance, and group frequency columns.

file

Character string indicating the output .xlsx filename or path. Default: "Tabella_sinottica.xlsx".

min_frequency

Numeric value between 0 and 100 specifying the minimum percentage frequency for retaining non-diagnostic species. Diagnostic species are retained regardless of this value. Default: 0.

digits

Non-negative integer indicating the number of decimal places displayed for species frequencies. Default: 0.

group_sizes

Optional named vector or table giving the number of vegetation relevés in each group, with names such as G1, G2, etc. When provided, a row showing group sample sizes is added to the Excel table. Default: NULL.

Value

Invisibly returns a data frame containing the exported species with Species, group frequency columns, Diagnostic_group, Phi, p_value, Dominant_in, max_freq, and section_order. It also writes an Excel workbook to the path specified by file.

Details

The input should be the synoptic component returned by synoptic_table(). The function does not calculate diagnostic species, frequency, or dominance; it formats and exports previously calculated results.

The input must contain the columns group, species, diagnostic, phi, p.value, and dominant, as well as frequency columns named GG1, GG2, etc. (corresponding to group labels G1, G2, etc.). Frequencies in these columns are percentages. Group columns are displayed in numerical order.

Diagnostic species are assigned to the section for their group with the highest Phi value. If a species is diagnostic for more than one group, the corresponding frequency cells may be highlighted in each group, even though the species appears in only one diagnostic section. Non-diagnostic species are included when their maximum frequency across groups is at least min_frequency. Diagnostic species are always retained, regardless of this threshold.

The Excel workbook contains two worksheets:

  • Synoptic_table: a formatted table organized by diagnostic group, followed by a section of other frequent species.

  • Original_data: the complete input table, without the export filter.

The output file is overwritten if it already exists. The function requires the openxlsx package.

References

Guarino, R., Caldarella, O., Gristina, A. S., Marcenò, C., & Gianguzzi, L. (2026). Broom-dominated shrublands of Sicily: revisiting the syntaxonomy of the Cytisetea scopario-striati at the south-eastern margin of their range. Vegetation Classification and Survey, 7, 127-148. https://doi.org/10.3897/VCS.183815

See also

synoptic_table(), openxlsx::createWorkbook()

Examples

# Example with a small, already calculated synoptic table
example_synoptic <- data.frame(
  group = c("G1", "G2", "G1"),
  species = c("Festuca rubra", "Bromus erectus", "Trifolium repens"),
  diagnostic = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE),
  phi = c(0.65, 0.58, NA),
  p.value = c(0.002, 0.010, NA),
  dominant = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
  GG1 = c(90, 25, 60),
  GG2 = c(15, 85, 55)
)

if (requireNamespace("openxlsx", quietly = TRUE)) {
  output_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
  exported <- export_synoptic(
    synoptic = example_synoptic,
    file = output_file,
    min_frequency = 30,
    group_sizes = c(G1 = 5, G2 = 6)
  )
  unlink(output_file)
}
#> Tabella sinottica esportata: /tmp/RtmpCMaFAe/file1ae5399f6273.xlsx
